$comment: The measured ink/surface table behind `azeebo-custom/no-low-contrast-pair`.
One rule, one table: a new solid fill is an entry here, not a new rule.
Each entry names a design token (`--color-az-<token>`) and the colour the
generated theme paints for it. The rule derives both spellings a page can
write — `bg-az-<token>` and `bg-[var(--color-az-<token>)]` — and computes
the WCAG 2.2 ratio from the two hex values, so no ratio is ever hand-typed
and stale. scripts/__tests__/no-low-contrast-pair.test.mjs re-reads every
hex here from apps/web/src/styles/design-tokens.css and fails when the two
drift, and it asserts the invariant the rule relies on: every fill that
enforces a floor must have a deep ink that clears it.
Which entries matter: the rule enforces only the pairings whose white ink
falls under `thresholds.bodyText`. The rest are listed because they are
measured too — `bg-az-scarlet` (4.69:1), `bg-az-primary-500` (4.69:1) and
`bg-az-error-600` (4.83:1) pass, so white ink there is deliberate and a
reviewer can see that rather than wondering whether the rule missed them.
The five semantic ramps are listed at every step a solid fill can be
written from (300–700); a chip, pill, swatch or button cannot slip through
on a step nobody remembered. Brand flame/scarlet, the reward-tier metals
and the categorical violets complete the set.
Adding a fill: add the token and its hex from the generated stylesheet.
Do not add translucent fills (`bg-az-flame/15`): they sit on the dark
canvas and keep the light ink on purpose, and the rule skips them by
design.

light.role: Tailwind's own white; the same pixel, a different utility

deep.role: the root surface ink — what every light fill should carry
Tailwind black; the same intent as the root surface ink

surfaces.note: Brand flame — light end of the CTA gradient; chips, tabs, compact CTAs.
Brand scarlet — white passes at 4.69:1; listed so the pass is visible.
Primary CTA red — white passes at 4.69:1, unlike its flame neighbour.
Blue — links, info states, `standard` bundle and carrier swatches.
Green — success states and completed step markers.
Amber — warnings, ratings, `ultimate` bundle and tier swatches; the worst pairing in the app at 2.15:1.
The destructive-fill step that keeps white ink lawful (4.83:1).
Reward-tier gold; also the offline banner fill.
Categorical premium hue — `premium` tier swatches, genre badges.
The lighter categorical violet step, used on selected dark rows.
